```python
import pytest
from your_application import SymptomsModule, authenticate_user

@pytest.fixture
def authenticated_user():
    # Implement user authentication and return an authenticated user object
    return authenticate_user()

@pytest.mark.parametrize("symptom_name, symptom_description", [
    ("Headache", "A constant, throbbing pain in the head"),
    ("Fever", "Elevated body temperature above normal"),
    # Add more symptom descriptions as needed
])
def test_add_symptom(authenticated_user, symptom_name, symptom_description):
    symptom = SymptomsModule(authenticated_user)
    symptom.add_symptom(symptom_name, symptom_description)
    assert symptom.is_added()

@pytest.mark.parametrize("symptom_id, new_description", [
    (1, "A constant, throbbing pain in the head with a slight ringing in the ears"),
    # Add more symptom IDs and descriptions as needed
])
def test_update_symptom(authenticated_user, symptom_id, new_description):
    symptom = SymptomsModule(authenticated_user)
    symptom.update_symptom(symptom_id, new_description)
    assert symptom.is_updated()

@pytest.mark.parametrize("symptom_id", [1])
def test_delete_symptom_valid_precondition(authenticated_user, symptom_id):
    symptom = SymptomsModule(authenticated_user)
    with pytest.raises(ExpectedException):  # Replace ExpectedException with the specific exception you expect
        symptom.delete_symptom(symptom_id)

@pytest.mark.parametrize("symptom_id", [1])
def test_delete_symptom_invalid_precondition(authenticated_user, symptom_id):
    symptom = SymptomsModule(authenticated_user)
    symptom.mark_used_in_consultation(symptom_id)  # This should raise an exception if the symptom has been used
    with pytest.raises(ExpectedException):
        symptom.delete_symptom(symptom_id)
```
